title: Inside a single cell
narration: Start with a single cell, the basic building block. Most electric cars use lithium-ion cells, and each one has the same few parts. On one side is the anode, usually made of graphite. On the other side is the cathode, a metal oxide that holds lithium. Between them sits a liquid called the electrolyte, which lets lithium move through it. And a thin plastic sheet, the separator, keeps the two sides from touching, because if they touched, the cell would short circuit. That is the whole recipe: two sides, a path between them, and a wall that keeps them apart.
